title: Endpoint-Aware Workflows to Detect and Quantify Isoforms and Alternative Splicing by RNA Sequencing
content: Alternative splicing and transcript isoform diversity expand the regulatory information captured by transcriptome profiling beyond gene-level expression. However, the reliable detection and quantification of isoforms and alternative splicing using RNA sequencing is complex and not determined by a single platform or computational tool. It is a workflow-centered measurement problem in which the analytical endpoint, RNA integrity, enrichment and library construction, sequencing strategy, computational analysis, benchmarking, and validation jointly determine the confidence of a research finding. This review reframes transcript-resolved sequencing in terms of endpoint-aware workflows, distinguishing among isoform discovery, isoform quantification, splicing event detection, differential isoform expression, differential transcript usage, and differential alternative splicing events. We compare short-read, long-read, and hybrid sequencing strategies across the experimental and computational decisions that most strongly affect reliability. We further discuss RNA reference materials, matched reference datasets, quality metrics, and orthogonal validation as recurring elements of workflow evaluation. An endpoint-aware reliability framework can help transcript-resolved studies progress from feature detection to reproducible, benchmark-supported, and biologically interpretable inference.
